def: An agent that treats machine-learning engineering as a tree search over single-file scripts, with draft, debug and improve operators.
The tree whose nodes are candidate scripts with their results and whose edges are attempts to fix or improve them.
AIDE's three operators: write a new solution, repair a crashed one, or make one atomic change to a working one.
The rule that chooses which node to extend next; in AIDE it drafts, then debugs buggy leaves with some probability, otherwise improves the best node.
A search that keeps a change only if it strictly improves the score and otherwise reverts.
A benchmark of 18 fundamental machine-learning research tasks designed to compare research-agent strategies under a shared interface and budget.
An agent's gain over the baseline divided by the range between the best and worst possible scores, floored at zero.
A measure of how much improvement a run found per unit of distance travelled in code space; high means small changes pay.
A comparison of two methods on the same tasks and seeds, using the per-task differences.
